title: A guard refuses marking a PR ready through the GitHub MCP tool when no `merge N --ready` run was made on it
why:
Coordinator 05:50 CST Nov 15 (relayed; triage read neither PR). Option (b) of step ready-refreshes-records, not picked: the coordinator took (a), a record-only rewrite. Two incidents (relayed): #3255 marked ready by MCP at 04:25 CST and #3472 at 05:40 CST; each ready PR then met a stale records page at confirm, because the MCP mark skips the records step that `merge N --ready` runs. Why it waits: no second guard-worthy incident since the rewrite, and a cloud false-alarm risk (`--ready`'s own mark may be refused by GraphQL; the lane's read, unchecked). Kin: github-mcp-writes-judged (the guard judges GitHub MCP writes, todo), ci-wake-mcp-ready (done), runner-ready-mark-check-in. Cost of the guard unmeasured. Revisit if the rewrite does not stop the refusals (runner 10 reports any refusal on `merge N --ready` for #3255 and #3496).

SIGHTING 06:05 CST Nov 15 (coordinator, relayed; triage read no log): #3472's first ready mark ended in the records refusal (the same incident as above); its second ready mark (05:46) passed with the records commit pushed by the records step, and it merged 06:03:22 CST. How the second mark was made was not stated.

SIGHTING 06:06 CST Nov 15 (coordinator, from runner 10's log; relayed, read by neither coordinator nor triage): this weakens the case for this guard. `merge 3255 --ready` already printed the order (mark ready by MCP update_pull_request draft=false after the draft run shows, then `--confirm`); the skipped step was the cause of both refusals, so a fixed record text may be enough. Keep as low, later.
source: coordinator 05:50 CST Nov 15, relayed by triage
note: Low, later. Only if the record rewrite in ready-refreshes-records does not stop MCP ready marks that skip the records step. Two incidents relayed.
